detection_focus: Security policy drift from hardened baseline
Unexpected changes to local security database
forensic_artifacts: Event Log: Security Event ID 4719 (System audit policy changed)
Event Log: Security Event ID 4739 (Domain policy changed)

flags.purpose: Analyzes current security settings against security templates and reports configuration drift and weaknesses.
flags.security_use_case: Audit system security configuration against known-good baselines to identify policy violations.
flags.threat_detected: Weak password policies, excessive privileges, disabled auditing, insecure user rights assignments.
flags.risk_if_misused: May produce warnings for legitimate business deviations; requires expert interpretation.
flags.safe_followup: Document deviations; compare with approved baseline; plan remediation via /configure.

flags.purpose: Exports current security policy to INF file for backup, analysis, or deployment.
flags.security_use_case: Capture system security state for compliance, forensics, or baseline comparison.
flags.risk_if_misused: Exported file contains sensitive security configuration; must be stored securely.
flags.safe_followup: Review and archive securely; compare with hardened baseline; use for change tracking.

flags.purpose: Imports security configuration into database for later application.
flags.security_use_case: Prepare standardized hardened security policy for deployment.
flags.risk_if_misused: Incorrect policy may cause user or admin lockout after apply.
flags.safe_followup: Validate with /validate; test in non-production; apply using /configure.

flags.purpose: Applies security configuration to the system from INF file.
flags.security_use_case: Enforce hardened system security baseline to reduce attack surface.
flags.risk_if_misused: Overly strict policy can break services or lock administrators out.
flags.safe_followup: Always backup with /export first; monitor system after apply; keep rollback ready.

flags.purpose: Generates rollback INF to restore previous configuration if changes cause issues.
flags.security_use_case: Safety mechanism before applying major security changes.
flags.risk_if_misused: Rollback only valid for that exact state; later changes invalidate it.
flags.safe_followup: Store rollback securely; use /import and /configure if recovery needed.

flags.purpose: Validates syntax and structure of INF file before applying.
flags.threat_detected: Invalid or malformed policies that could cause unpredictable behavior.
flags.safe_followup: Proceed to /import and /configure if validation succeeds.

detection_queries.command: secedit /export /areas SECURITYPOLICY /cfg security_policy.inf && (Get-Content security_policy.inf | Findstr /i "MinimumPasswordLength PasswordComplexity LockoutBadCount")
detection_queries.why_powerful: Immediately verifies password and lockout policy compliance from live system export.
detection_queries.security_context: Detecting weakened credential policies used by attackers after privilege escalation.

detection_queries.why_powerful: Surfaces policy analysis problems and potential security misconfigurations quickly.
detection_queries.security_context: Rapid integrity assessment during incident response.

detection_queries.command: secedit /export /cfg baseline.inf /areas USER_RIGHTS && (Get-Content baseline.inf | Findstr /i "SeDebugPrivilege SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege")
detection_queries.why_powerful: Identifies dangerous privilege assignments often abused by attackers.

tool_relationship.attacker_usage: Attackers modify local security policy to weaken defenses, disable auditing, and grant dangerous privileges.
tool_relationship.defender_usage: Used for auditing, exporting, validating, and enforcing hardened security baselines across systems.
